description: Recommended Claude Code native-sandbox configuration. This is the DURABLE security boundary for Vajra — the pre-tool hook is defense-in-depth, the OS sandbox (macOS Seatbelt / Linux bubblewrap) is enforced at the syscall level and holds regardless of what command the model emits. Merge `settings` into ~/.claude/settings.json (or apply per-project in .claude/settings.json). NOTE: this file is a REFERENCE — Vajra never auto-writes settings.json (it is both the immutable core and a system-settings change). Run scripts/enable-sandbox.sh to print platform-checked apply instructions.
why: The native sandbox OS-denies writes to settings.json at every scope AND to a worktree's hooks/ and config — the enforced version of Vajra's immutable-core hook (VJR-01) and fleet confinement (VJR-04).
denyRead on credential dirs closes the secret-exfiltration leg of the lethal trifecta that a regex hook cannot reliably catch.
allowedDomains breaks egress so an injected agent cannot phone home — the boundary holds even if a command obfuscates past the hook denylist.
notes: failIfUnavailable: set to true for unattended / managed deployments so a missing sandbox is a hard failure, not a silent fallback to unsandboxed execution.
allowUnsandboxedCommands:false = Strict mode — the dangerouslyDisableSandbox escape hatch is ignored.
Default read policy still ALLOWS ~/.aws and ~/.ssh — the denyRead list above is required, not optional.

allowedDomains is a conservative dev default (package registries + GitHub). Tailor to your pipeline's exact hosts; the proxy matches hostname only and does NOT inspect TLS, so a broad domain like github.com can be domain-fronted — for high assurance use a TLS-terminating custom proxy (sandbox.network.httpProxyPort).
Linux/WSL2 require: bubblewrap + socat (apt/dnf install), and `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` for the seccomp Unix-socket filter. macOS needs nothing (Seatbelt is built in).
Enable interactively any time with the /sandbox command; managed-settings lockdown (allowManagedDomainsOnly, allowManagedReadPathsOnly) enforces it org-wide.
Never add a Unix socket like /var/run/docker.sock to allowUnixSockets — it grants host access and defeats the sandbox.
